title: An overview of memory management and the garbage collector

videos.script: Lesson 23 returned the address of a local variable and said that was safe. This lesson shows why. {{escape}} Every value in a Go program lives in one of two places. You never pick which. The compiler does, and it will print its reasons if you ask it. {{trace}} Then the garbage collector. It finds what your program can still reach and frees the rest, while the program keeps running. One environment variable makes it print a line for every collection, and you will read that line field by field. {{knobs}} Two settings decide how often it runs. GOGC trades memory for time. GOMEMLIMIT gives the runtime a ceiling to stay under. {{keep}} Last, memory that nobody leaked on purpose. Sixteen bytes of a slice can hold sixty-four megabytes in place, and one call lets them go. By the end you can look at a running Go program and say why it holds the memory it holds.
